gates: Read the full dashboard contract for application, integration, port, or release work
Focused Vitest tests for changed behavior; build/typecheck where relevant
UX: executable layout plan, mandatory manual image/interaction review, matching state and viewport coverage
Ports: Lovelace config/action mapping plus authorized real-browser parity
No production release without explicit authorization; preserve both HA hosts

always: Keep secrets out of evidence and preserve user changes.
Home Assistant owns state changes and cascading effects; research grants no live-operation authority.

research: Use actual shared components and HA service boundaries as evidence; do not infer runtime/browser behavior from source alone.
EverShelf access belongs behind HA services, with ranking/filtering owned by its backend.
implementation: Read the full dashboard contract and matching scoped instructions before changes.
validation: Use the affected tests and executable layout plan; required manual image/state review is not replaceable by source inspection.
release: Explicit release-dashboard scope review and both HA hosts remain required; the disabled version 3 machine permits no GitHub, HA, or deployment execution.

commands.layout: npm run layout:check; use docs/ux/layouts.md for plan/run/verify arguments
commands.release: Explicit release-dashboard preflight only while the deterministic machine is disabled
